h: Plan for smaller budgets but a larger share for clothing
b: Every major 2026 survey shows holiday budgets falling: RCC/Leger $911, down 6.5%; Deloitte down 14% to a record low; PwC down 11%; Accenture gifts down nearly 4%. Clothing is the exception. It rises to 19% of RCC budgets from 17%, and 47% of Accenture respondents plan to buy clothing and accessories. Fight for share of wallet rather than expecting the total to grow.

h: Black Friday is still the main event, and Cyber Monday is catching up
b: 88% rank Black Friday in their top three days and 52% rank it first. Cyber Monday's top-three share jumps to 72% from 64%. Each takes about 29% of budgets, and 51% of budgets will be spent by the end of BFCM. In 2025, Black Friday was the single busiest card day. Weight media and inventory to the full 27 to 30 Nov window rather than one day.

h: Start earlier, because shoppers already have
b: 81% plan to start before BFCM, up from 47%, even as 43% hold purchases for big sale days. In 2025, Canadian online sales were already up 12% to 13% in the first two weeks of November at 28% average discounts. Use early-access drops and price-match messaging so early shoppers do not wait, and so you do not train them to.

78% will actively seek deals. 69% are trading down to cheaper alternatives. The 2025 BFCM weekend averaged 30% off in Canadian online. Footwear prices are already falling: CPI -0.8% YoY and nominal footwear sales -4.0% while volumes rose 10.2%. Use deep cuts on hero franchises and bundles, and protect margin elsewhere.

h: Gen Z is the growth cohort, and it shops BFCM
b: Gen Z is the only generation raising budgets, by 8%, and 38% plan to shop Black Friday weekend. Reviews matter to 90% of 18 to 34 year olds. Note the youth job market is weakening, with 15 to 24 employment down 48,000 in September, so value framing and BNPL still matter.

h: Stores still win, so plan omnichannel
b: 58% of RCC budgets go to stores, 55% per Deloitte, and 83% of Canadians expect to shop in physical stores, with 38% of spend hybrid. 62% want to see and touch products, which matters for fit-sensitive footwear. Push buy online pick up in store, store inventory visibility in ads, and in-store-only doorbusters. Online is still growing fast: e-commerce was up 15.3% YoY in August.

h: Lead with Buy Canadian and "not American" messaging, but carefully
b: 84% favour Made in Canada gifts, but 52% add "if the price is reasonable". 54% would pay more for Canadian-made, and 61% are buying more Canadian goods. A mostly US-brand footwear assortment is exposed: 58% of trade-affected shoppers avoid US brands. Canada's counter-tariffs include 50% on US clothing from 8 Sep. Audit which SKUs are US-made versus Asia-made under US brands, and spotlight Canadian brands and non-US product origin where accurate.

h: Cross-border leakage is down, so there is an opening to win back Canadians
b: Cross-border holiday shopping intent fell to 13% from 20% in 2024. With US tariffs and counter-tariffs in place, domestic retailers have a pricing and convenience edge.

Planned AI use is rising: 39% per Deloitte, 31% per RCC, 28% per PwC. Deal-finding is the top use at 40%. In 2025, AI and agents influenced 21% of Canadian Cyber Week orders. Clean product feeds, structured pricing and price-comparison-friendly content will matter for being surfaced.

h: Shipping risk is lower than in 2024 and 2025, but cutoffs are early
b: The Canada Post contract now runs to Jan 2029, unlike the 2024 national strike and the 2025 rotating strikes. Canada Post national ground cutoff is Dec 10 and Xpresspost is Dec 22. Weekend parcel delivery reaches Toronto and Montreal by late November. Shipping costs are expected to be about 7% higher. Message cutoffs from Cyber Week onward.

h: Mobile and payments: optimise mobile checkout and offer BNPL
b: In 2025, mobile drove 63% of Canadian Cyber Week orders, mobile wallets were 18% of payments, and BNPL doubled to 5% of transactions. 31% of Canadians say they are willing to use BNPL for BFCM 2026. Feature Apple Pay, Google Pay and pay-in-4 on product pages for higher-ticket sneakers.

h: The macro picture is getting worse, so frame value through December
b: The Bank of Canada hiked to 2.5% on 28 Oct. Inflation is 3.1%, 68,000 jobs were lost in September, and Signal49 says confidence slipped further in October. Still, August retail sales rose 1.2% and sporting goods retailers grew 5.1% YoY. Plan for a careful, deal-driven shopper rather than a spending collapse. Dec 22 and 23 rivalled Black Friday volume in 2025, so keep a strong last-minute in-store and gift card play.
